metadata.name: dsh-tools-toggle

paragraphs.text: Toggle DeepSeek Harness (DSH) model tools on/off from the web Settings page — hidden tools lose sche
ma, lookup, and execution together
# dsh-tools-toggle
**Turn DeepSeek Harness (DSH) model tools on and off with a switch, from the web Settings page.** Ev
ery inherited tool — `bash`, `web_search`, `web_fetch`, whatever your presets and plugins add — show
s up as one row with a toggle. Flip it off and the tool disappears from the model's view entirely: n
o schema in the request, no description in the prompt, no execution on call. Flip it back on and the
next session gets it again.
## Why
DSH gives agents a fixed tool surface, and every tool on it costs tokens on every request and invite
s the model to reach for it. Sometimes you want less: a session that never touches the network, a fo
cused agent without the noise of twenty irrelevant tools, or a quick A/B of whether a tool is helpin
g at all. The built-in answer was hand-editing the profile patch and restarting.
dsh-tools-toggle is that switch, in the UI, with one click — and it removes the tool from the model'
s *knowledge*, not just its permissions, so the tokens go away too.
## How it works
1. **Settings → Tools** — the plugin mounts a section in the native Settings page: the full catalog
of inherited tools (preset-plane tools included), each with its name, one-line description, a search

box, and a "disabled only" filter.
2. **Persistence through config** — a toggle POSTs to the plugin
's host route, which writes the deny list into the plugin's Loader-entry config via the settings ser
vice. The change lands in the profile patch (user layer), so it survives upgrades. Writes are serial
ized so rapid toggles never stack on a stale base, and reads wait for pending writes (read-your-writ

es).
3. **Hiding via restriction** — the host half applies the list by calling `agent.ctx.tools.rest
rict({ deny })` once per agent. A denied tool loses schema, lookup, and execution *together* — the w
eakest mechanism that still removes it — so the model never learns it existed. Guessing the name any
way gets a clean `UNKNOWN_TOOL` rejection.
### The creation-time snapshot
A restriction rewrites the model-facing tool array, which is part of the request prefix — applying i
t to a *live* conversation would invalidate the provider prefix cache from the first changed token.
So the deny list is applied **when an agent is created**, and never touched afterward:

- New sessions (and new subagents) get the current toggle state.
- Existing conversations keep their

tool surface — and their cache — until they naturally end.
- A host restart resumes sessions as new
agents, so changes made between boots apply on resume (one unavoidable re-prefill).
### What can't be broken
- **Scope-local machinery is exempt by construction** — subagent delegation's structured-output plum
bing and the reserved PTC `run_code` transport are never toggleable, so workflows and multi-agent se

tups keep running.
- **You can't lock yourself out** — the toggle state lives in the UI, not in the

tools, so even with every switch off the Settings page still works and restores everything.
- **Core
tools ask first** — disabling `bash`, `read`, `write`, or `edit` pops a one-time confirm dialog.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Refresh DSH Web and open **Settings → Tools** (Korean and English locales included).
Plain ESM, no build step. Peers (`cordis`, `dsh-tools`, `dsh-host-webserver`) resolve from the DSH i
nstall tree; for a link-based dev setup, symlink `node_modules` to the DSH installation's own `node_
modules`, since `pnpm link:` cannot resolve peers by itself.
## Notes & limitations
- **New sessions only.** Live conversations are deliberately untouched — that's the prefix-cache pro

tection, not a bug.
- **The catalog needs a session.** Tool names are snapshotted from live agents,

so before the first session the page shows a "start a session" hint.
- **Profile-wide, not per-sessi

on.** One deny list for the whole profile; per-session overrides are future work.
- **Toggle UI only
, no agent tool.** Re-enabling is policy relaxation, so it stays human-only by design.
